sections.title: The market today
sections.body: About 174,000 US children are diagnosed with Tourette syndrome (~1 in 333, 0.3%), but roughly half of all cases go undiagnosed — implying ~1 in 162 children (0.6%) are truly affected. It is a large, under-identified pediatric population managed today with decades-old generic antipsychotics and off-label alpha-2 agonists.

sections.title: The patient journey
sections.body: Families consult about four different clinicians over years before diagnosis; care concentrates in pediatric neurology and child psychiatry and is mediated by caregivers and schools. The bottleneck is diagnosis and specialist access — not treatment capacity.

sections.title: Who treats it — and how
sections.body: Only three drugs are FDA-approved for tics (haloperidol, pimozide, aripiprazole — all D2 antipsychotics with EPS and metabolic liabilities), while real-world first-line care leans on behavioral therapy (CBIT) and off-label generic alpha-2 agonists. Everything effective today is either old, off-label, or hard to access.

sections.title: The economic opportunity
sections.body: Third-party analysts size the TS treatment market at roughly $2.0–2.7B, a base that is largely generic today; a differentiated, on-label branded entrant is the value-creation opportunity, with sell-side peak-sales estimates for ecopipam of up to ~$1B. (External estimates — this tool does not model revenue.)

sections.title: What's missing — why it's worth pursuing
sections.body: The guideline ladder pushes antipsychotics down for tolerability, first-line CBIT is throttled by a therapist shortage, and no new mechanism has arrived in over a decade — leaving experts, patients, and caregivers with options that are effective-but-toxic or effective-but-inaccessible. A weight-neutral, non-antipsychotic mechanism with positive Phase 3 data — now accepted by FDA for Priority Review — is the first credible answer to that gap.

one_liner: A large, under-served pediatric market with no modern mechanism — and a first-in-class, non-antipsychotic asset with positive Phase 3 data, four months from an FDA decision.

timeline.label: Teva agrees to acquire Emalex ($700M upfront)

whats_new.text: New Current treatment view: FDA label status, boxed warnings, supply notices, adverse event reports, Medicaid prescription volume and evidence depth for 12 agents in use today, plus open registered studies and specialist counts by state.
FDA accepted the ecopipam NDA and granted Priority Review; target action date is late Q1 2027. The proposed indication is pediatric-only.

New MDS data: ~70% of participants reached a clinically meaningful tic reduction within 8 weeks (post hoc), and the open-label extension showed a 45.6% mean tic-severity reduction at 18 months with no new safety signals.
Gemlapodect's Phase 2b topline is overdue — registry primary completion was estimated June 2026 and no readout has been located.
SCI-110 Phase 2b sites activated (Hannover, Yale) and European drug batch released; adults only.
Neupulse launched in the UK as a 'wellness' wrist device; the medical version is still in regulatory development, with no FDA clearance.
University of Minnesota's MnTiC Lab designated a TAA Center of Excellence — the network now exceeds the 28 counted in Feb 2025.
CDC prevalence figures re-checked: still ~174,000 diagnosed children (1 in 333) and ~1 in 162 true prevalence, on 2016–2019 data. Rare Pediatric Disease / voucher status remains unconfirmed.
